project.topic: Why most AI features ship as demos and never become real products

insights.insight: Demos optimize for a single happy path; products require tail behavior to be acceptable.
insights.why_it_matters: Tail behavior is what users hit on day three.

angles.title: Demos are not products
angles.thesis: AI features die when teams ship demos and stop building once the gif looks good.
angles.hook: Most AI features die at the demo line.

thread_items.text: Most AI features die at the demo line. The gif looks good, the launch tweet ships, and the feature quietly stops mattering.
Demos optimize one happy path. Products survive the long tail: weird inputs, unclear intent, partial answers.
Real AI products look boring from the outside: evaluation harnesses, retry logic, fallbacks, escalation rules, and a humble UI that admits failure.
A simple rule: if the only screenshot of the feature is its best case, you have a demo. If you can show the third worst case and explain how the system behaves, you have a product.
The bar for AI features in 2026 is not 'can it impress'. It is 'can it be relied on'. That is a different engineering problem.

items.claim: Most AI features die at the demo line.
